title: The case for vertical BIPV
content:
A major IEA PVPS Task 15 study finds that vertical BIPV façades can complement rooftop solar with minimal yield penalties, smoothing generation across the day while offering greater design flexibility. Across 357 configurations in 44 cities, the research also shows BIPV economics improve substantially when avoided building-material costs are counted, with long-term viability shaped by electricity prices, financing, installation costs, and application type.

title: Scientists propose solar cell taxonomy based on absorber integration
content:
Researchers in Spain have proposed a new photovoltaic taxonomy that replaces the conventional generation-based approach with a classification based on absorber integration and dominant physical mechanisms. The framework divides solar technologies into four groups—wafer-based, thin-film, epitaxial III–V, and sensitized or quantum-confined systems—while also providing a flexible way to classify tandem and hybrid architectures.

title: Solar surpasses nuclear power globally for first time
content: Solar and wind are increasingly outpacing nuclear power globally, with solar generation surpassing nuclear for the first time in 2025, according to WNISR 2026. The report highlights nuclear’s slow growth, lengthy construction timelines and limited small modular reactor deployment, contrasting them with rapid renewables and battery expansion.

title: U.S. team claims stability record for 16.19%-efficient 2D/3D tin perovskite solar cell
content: U.S. researchers developed a 2D/3D lead-free tin perovskite solar cell using a chlorinated spacer, achieving 16.19% efficiency while improving crystallinity and resistance to oxygen and moisture. The device retained 95% of its initial efficiency after more than 1,600 hours in dry air and 80% after 1,000 hours under continuous illumination at 55 C.
